messages.content: Find state law cases related to land disputes in the past 5 years from 2015 to 2021 in New York.

function.name: law_case_search
function.description: Search and retrieve law cases based on the topic, timeline, and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

topic.description: The subject matter of the case.

year_range.description: The start and end year for searching cases.

location.description: The location where the case is being heard.

judicial_system.description: The specific judicial system in which to search (e.g. 'federal', 'state').

So we need to search for cases in New York state courts, presumably. The user says "past 5 years from 2015 to 2021". That is a bit confusing: 2015 to 2021 is 7 years. But maybe they mean "past 5 years" relative to 2021? Actually, the user says "past 5 years from 2015 to 2021". That might be a mistake. But we can interpret as "cases from 2015 to 2021 inclusive" or "cases from 2015 to 2021 inclusive" but that is 7 years. But maybe they want "cases from 2015 to 2021 inclusive" but only the last 5 years? That would be 2017 to 2021. But the user explicitly says "from 2015 to 2021". So we should search for cases from 2015 to 2021 inclusive. The user also says "state law cases related to land disputes". So we need to search for cases in New York state courts. The user wants "state law cases" meaning not federal. So we set judicial_system to "state". The location is "New York". The topic is "land disputes". The year_range is [2015, 2021]. So we call the function law_case_search with those parameters.
